title: lua: ByteArray integer parsing APIs
description:
Adds APIs for parsing different kinds of integer from a lua ByteArray:
-16, 32 and 64 bit
-signed or unsigned
-encoded little endian or big endian

@Developer-Alexander Why can't you use the generic `ByteArray:tvb():range()` to get the integers? This looks like very specific methods which can be solved using existing methods.

Example to get a int16 from offset 2 in a byte array:
```
ba = ByteArray.new("00010042")
integer = ba:tvb():range(2,2):int()
```

Update: Fixed in !9342

Looks like `make-wsluarm.py` is expecting the `#define` to use the name of the method it is located in.

[wslua_byte_array.c](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/epan/wslua/wslua_byte_array.c#L227):  
```
WSLUA_METHOD ByteArray_get_le_int16(lua_State* L) {
    /* Read a little endian encoded 16 bit signed integer in a <<lua_class_ByteArray,`ByteArray`>> beginning at given index.

    @since 4.1.0
    */
#define WSLUA_ARG_ByteArray_get_index_INDEX 2 /* The position of the first byte. */
```

[docbook/make-wsluarm.py](https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/blob/master/docbook/make-wsluarm.py#L150):  
```

        if id != self.id:

            sys.exit(1)
```

Note that I am considiering to revert this commit because I think we already have the needed functionality using `TvbRange`. I will wait for a response from @Developer-Alexander first.

> `ba:tvb():range(2,2):int()`
I think that is not a very intuitive solution for a quite common problem when dealing with ByteArrays.

And I don‘t know how the performance compares. Is it costly to create a TVB and a Range?

We can probably add `ByteArray:range()` to be able to shorten this to `ba:range(2,2):int()`.
In general I don't like multiple implementations to do the same.

Is this really a common problem dealing with ByteArrays? Do you have any examples? You should not need to convert packet data to ByteArray before extracting integers because you use `Tvb` and `TvbRange`. What about other types like `float`, `string`, `time`, etc.? And none of our existing methods use the "get_" prefix.

I have no idea about performance, the conversions requires some small malloc's, but it's mostly offset/length and no calculations. Maybe you are able to do some measurements?

> Is this really a common problem dealing with ByteArrays? Do you have any examples?

I use ByteArray to perform some manual desegmentation of segmented data. I collect the data in ByteArrays and created new TVB when I have enough data for valid message. For determining the length I need the possibility to read 32 big endian integer for example.

> What about other types like `float`, `string`, `time`, etc.?

In general I would say the API should be aligned with TVB. You should be able to do the same with a ByteArray as you could do with a TVB regarding reading data. So I would consider this as a first step in this direction.

> And none of our existing methods use the "get\_" prefix.

The naming should be aligned for consistency ofc.

> Maybe you are able to do some measurements?

I will do a simple comparison.

One disadvantage of using `ByteArray:tvb():range()` is that it is only available in a dissector but not during init phase.

![grafik](/uploads/2eaf2033ba10d1ed6ba4b2c8e8d27351/grafik.png)

On the other hand using `ByteArray:tvb():range():int()` seems to be roughly 419 times slower in my short test of 100000 read operations.

- range: 6,290000 s
- get_le_int32: 0,015000 s


```
local data = ByteArray.new("11 22 33 44 55 66 77 88 99")


tap = Listener.new(nil, "frame")

function tap.packet(pinfo, tvb, tapdata)

    local startTime = 0.0
    local endTime = 0.0
    local duration = endTime - startTime

    startTime = os.clock()

    local integer = 0
    for i = 1, 100000 do
        integer = data:tvb():range(2, 4):int()
    end

    endTime = os.clock();
    duration = endTime - startTime

    report_failure(string.format("range: %f s", duration))

    startTime = os.clock()
    for i = 1, 100000 do
        integer = data:get_le_int32(2)
    end
    endTime = os.clock();
    duration = endTime - startTime

    report_failure(string.format("get_le_int32: %f s", duration))

end
```
How to proceed?

I will suggest two changes:
1. Remove the `get_` prefix and rename `index` to `offset`. This will align with the TvbRange methods.
2. Change the APIs to `(le_)?u?int(offset, length)` for 1 to 4 bytes and `(le_)?u?int64(offset, length)` for 1 to 8 bytes. This makes the API more generic.

The first and second suggestion is done in !11757.

@Developer-Alexander Unfortunately we don't have any unit tests for this API so it's hard to verify the refactoring, so please have a look.
When adding unit tests I found a bug handling negative integers.

Another alternative is to use the `ByteArray:subset()` method to select offset and length, and then use `uint()` etc. on the subset. Like `data:subset(0,4):uint()`. I'll have a look at also supporting this.
